title: The Gingerbread Man
author: Sara Cone Bryant; adapted for Shellfie
credit: From Project Gutenberg eBook #473 (public domain in the US). A shortened, gentle adaptation for young readers; the ending has been changed.

pages: An old woman baked a gingerbread boy.
She opened the oven. Out he jumped!
The gingerbread boy ran out the door.
“Run, run!” he called. “Can you catch me?”
A cow saw him. She ran after him.
A horse saw him. He ran after him too.
The gingerbread boy came to a wide river.
A fox offered to help him cross.
“Hold on,” said the fox. “I can swim.”
The gingerbread boy rode on the fox’s back.
They reached the other side, safe and dry.
“Thank you!” said the boy. His friends waved from shore.
The fox swam back with him. Everyone shared a picnic.

quiz.q: Who helped the gingerbread boy cross the river?
quiz.ev: A fox offered to help him cross.

quiz.q: Why did the gingerbread boy ride on the fox’s back?
o: He wanted to take a nap
The fox wanted to play a song
